text: DSH Side Tasks 是面向网页客户端的侧边任务插件。在主会话标题栏加入任务入口和数量提示，并在页面覆盖层显示当前会话的任务列表与对话面板。宿主能力可用时，它会从主会话 fork 子会话，提供独立任务消息的发送、停止、历史查看与删除，并按活动时间管理一小时闲置清理；任务关联信息保存在浏览器本地。适合希望把临时工作拆到独立子会话、又想从主对话旁快速切换的人。目标 DSH 需提供历史与删除能力，缺少时新建和删除会被禁用。

DSH Side Tasks adds a task button and panel to the web client. It uses host-supported child sessions to keep temporary work separate, with controls to read, send, and stop task messages. Task references are stored locally. Hosts without history or deletion support disable task creation and deletion.

DSH Side Tasks 的功能「侧边任务面板」：在会话标题栏提供任务入口和数量标记，打开后显示当前主会话关联的子任务。用户可收起为角落中的任务数提示，再展开面板。
DSH Side Tasks 的功能「创建与对话」：在支持所需宿主能力时，用户新建任务会从当前会话 fork 子会话；选中任务后可发送文本、查看任务自身的用户和助手消息，并停止正在运行的轮次。
DSH Side Tasks 的功能「任务保存与过期」：任务列表和活动时间按主会话写入浏览器本地存储；后台周期检查非运行中的任务，闲置满一小时后尝试删除。
DSH Side Tasks 的功能「删除任务」：点击任务删除后需再次确认；宿主删除成功时，面板移除任务和本地关联，删除失败则保留条目并显示错误。
DSH Side Tasks 使用前须知：固定版本兼容说明指出目标 DSH 缺少可验证的完整删除接口时会禁用创建、删除与自动清理；安装前需确认宿主提供所需能力。

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks README · @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Side tasks plugin, browser half: a temporary per-session task panel beside the main conversation. The conversation header gains a 「侧边任务」 action with a live count badge; clicking it opens a right-hand overlay panel owned by the current session, which **collapses to a compact top-right chip** as its resting state and expands while a task is being worked on.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks README · @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks：Each side task is a **forked child session** (`session.fork` with title incrementation) — it runs its own agent with the owner's full context, independent of the main thread. Two properties make it a temporary task rather than a fork visible in the sidebar:

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks README · @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks：- **Hidden by default**: the child is archived (`workspace.archiveSession`) right after creation, so it never appears in the workspace sidebar or the ungrouped bucket — the panel is its only surface. The forked seed context is the task's working memory, not its display: the mini conversation shows only the task's OWN messages (everything after the task's LAST `session/end-seed` marker — an owner that was itself resumed or forked nests earlier markers inside the seed, so the first one would leak the owner's recent messages), so a new task is just a composer ready to talk.
- **Self-expiring**: a task with no activity (creation, send, or a settled turn) for one hour (`SIDE_TASK_TTL_MS`) is deleted automatically by the apply-side sweep while the page is open; persisted activity timestamps let a refresh resume the same expiry. Running tasks are never swept. Each task row shows its own live countdown (`还剩 N 分钟自动删除`, ticking every second from the persisted last-activity timestamp) so the expiry is never a surprise.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks README · @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks：The lifecycle is the plugin's core selling point: **deleting a task leaves no residue**. The delete button (two-click confirm) calls `session.delete(childId)`, which disposes the host agent, removes the child from every workspace account, and erases its stored log — the task row, the panel selection, and the persisted collection entry all go with it. Closing the panel only hides the UI: tasks and their idle agents stay alive until their expiry sweep and reappear on reopen.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks README · Slot and data architecture：Two registrations share one apply-owned controller (a register-declared store mounts under exactly one scope, so cross-scope sharing goes through the controller):

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks README · Slot and data architecture：- **`conversation.session.header.actions`** (session scope, id `side-task`, order 30): the trigger button + count badge. Reads the store through the injected `useSideTasks` hook; the owner passes nothing.
- **`shell.overlay`** (root scope, id `side-task-panel`): the right-hand panel OR the collapsed chip. Reads the store (`useSideTasks`), the selected task's conversation (`useTaskConversation` — a derived source that follows the store's `selected` binding), the session list (`useSessions`), and the injected verbs (create/delete/send/stop/select/collapse/expand/close).

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks README · Slot and data architecture：The controller owns the `createSnapshotStore` instance, the conversation source, per-session localStorage persistence (ids + per-task activity timestamps), the expiry sweep, and the RPC verbs; components receive everything through the inject face and never touch `ctx`.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks README · Model Experience：Indirectly, through the `session.fork`, `session.prompt`, `session.cancel`, and `session.delete` verbs the panel invokes: creating a task forks a child session from the current session's prefix with an incremented title, sending a prompt queues a user turn in the task's own session, stopping cancels its running turn, and deleting removes the child's log and workspace accounts. The panel itself adds no prompt content of its own; everything the model sees comes from the user's own sends inside a task.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks README · KV Cache effect：None from the plugin itself. Sending inside a task extends that child session's history tail like any other prompt, so admitted context can change its provider-side cache reuse; deleting a task removes its log entirely.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- **Mini-conversation is text-only** — tool calls, context injections, reasoning blocks, and other surface nodes are intentionally omitted from the compact panel; the full transcript lives in the main conversation by opening the task session normally.
- **Expiry sweep runs while the page is open** — a task left idle with the browser closed stays until the next page load (the persisted activity timestamps resume the countdown then); there is no host-side janitor. — the event window only backfills the current session, so the panel fetches the selected task's durable history (`session.history`) on selection and refreshes when a running turn settles or after a send. A reply in progress shows a 「运行中」 indicator and appears in full once the turn ends.
- **Panel is single-owner** — it follows the current session (`useSessions.current`); switching sessions re-points the panel to the new owner's collection. There is no multi-pane side-task view.
- **Queued sends while running are disabled** — the composer locks during a running turn instead of offering the main composer's queue semantics; a task must settle be

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks README · Installation：The repository ships prebuilt bundles (`lib/`), so a normal user installs
in two steps — no build toolchain needed:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/uluckystar/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-client-ui-side-tasks   # or your active profile

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks README · restart the profile for the bundle metadata to take effect：**Standalone activation (MyDSH rc.6)**: the package includes a `dsh.bundle`
patch that mounts its inert host entry. That registration is required for DSH to
discover and load the browser module; a plain dependency installation alone is
not proof of activation. Restart the profile, then verify that the browser loaded
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks/client.js` and the session header shows the
side-task action. Some DSH builds already include a side-task UI: remove the
other registration before enabling a duplicate.

不同 DSH 版本的客户端注入和槽位接口可能变化。安装前请在独立 profile 验证任务创建、主子会话归属、停止、删除与重载；仓库元数据或声明校验通过不能代替这些实测。

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks README · Fixed-version validation and capability boundary：On DSH source commit `99f6f02fecdb7dff40c3fbc9470f5907c29f74ca` (CLI rc.7),
a clean isolated profile confirms installation, host-layer registration and
browser-module loading. That runtime does **not** expose the legacy client
`ctx.sessions.history` / `ctx.sessions.delete` methods this plugin's temporary
lifecycle requires. rc.6 therefore disables creation/deletion and explains the
missing capability instead of creating children that cannot be cleaned up or
throwing a browser TypeError. This is **not** a passing full lifecycle test on
that DSH version. Do not rely on one-hour expiry there.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks README · rc.7: read existing history through the declared wire API：The pinned DSH build does expose `connection.api.sessions.history` even though
the older `ctx.sessions.history` helper is absent. rc.7 adapts that read-only
method, preserving pagination and RPC errors. Legacy business rejection never
triggers a second-path retry. Existing task history can be displayed without
creating a new child, and the owner's fork seed remains hidden.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks README · rc.8: operation acknowledgements and current declarations：Failed or malformed send/stop RPC results and missing bindings no longer look
like success. Failed sends preserve the current composer draft and activity
time; pending submissions are not duplicated, and a late acknowledgement does
not erase newer edits or another selected task's draft. Acknowledgement is not
a model-completion or durable-transcript guarantee.
